topicName: RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) and DPO
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Technical Tutorial: RLHF and DPO in Natural Language Processing"},{"order":2,"type":"subheading","text":"Introduction"},{"order":3,"type":"paragraph","text":"Aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) with human preferences is critical for creating safe, helpful, and honest AI systems. While standard pre-training teaches models next-token prediction on massive corpora, and instruction tuning teaches them how to follow prompts, alignment ensures their outputs match human values. Two dominant paradigms for this alignment are Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)."},{"order":4,"type":"subheading","text":"Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF)"},{"order":5,"type":"paragraph","text":"RLHF is a multi-step training pipeline designed to optimize an LLM using human preference data. It involves three primary stages:"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"1. Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT): The base model is fine-tuned on a high-quality dataset of instructions and desired responses."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"2. Reward Modeling: A separate reward model is trained on human preference data to score responses based on helpfulness and safety."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"3. Reinforcement Learning: The LLM acts as an actor, generating responses evaluated by the reward model, typically optimized using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"The RLHF/PPO Optimization Loop"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"During the PPO phase, the policy model is updated based on rewards while penalizing deviation from the original SFT model using KL-divergence. A conceptual training step looks like this:"},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"import torch

# Conceptual PPO loss calculation with KL penalty
def compute_ppo_loss(policy_chosen_logps, ref_chosen_logps, rewards, kl_coef):
    kl = ref_chosen_logps - policy_chosen_logps
    loss = -(rewards - kl_coef * kl).mean()
    return loss"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"While RLHF is powerful, it is notoriously unstable and complex, requiring multiple models in memory simultaneously (the actor, reference model, critic, and reward model). Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), introduced by Rafailov et al., mathematically reformulates the RLHF objective to optimize the language model directly on preference data without a separate reward model."},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"DPO Loss Implementation"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"DPO uses binary cross-entropy loss to increase the likelihood of preferred completions while decreasing the likelihood of dispreferred completions. Here is a standard PyTorch implementation of the DPO loss function:"},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

def dpo_loss(policy_chosen_logps, policy_rejected_logps, reference_chosen_logps, reference_rejected_logps, beta=0.1):
    pi_logratios = policy_chosen_logps - policy_rejected_logps
    ref_logratios = reference_chosen_logps - reference_rejected_logps
    
    logits = pi_logratios - ref_logratios
    loss = -F.logsigmoid(beta * logits).mean()
    return loss"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Comparing RLHF and DPO"},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Complexity: RLHF requires training and hosting multiple models (Actor, Critic, Reward Model, Reference Model). DPO only requires the Policy Model and a frozen Reference Model."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Stability: RLHF is sensitive to hyperparameters, reward hacking, and unstable gradients. DPO uses standard cross-entropy loss, making it much more stable."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Performance: Empirically, DPO matches or exceeds the performance of traditional PPO-based RLHF while consuming significantly fewer compute resources."},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Both RLHF and DPO remain foundational pillars in modern NLP engineering. While RLHF pioneered alignment through reinforcement learning, DPO has largely democratized the process by turning alignment into a simple supervised classification task over paired preference data."}]
